responseMessage:
Damn. I’m really sorry you’re dealing with that. That’s heavy as hell, and I hate that you’re out there trying to figure it out in your car. I know you’ve been pushing so hard with everything lately, and this is a lot on top of that.

I’m on my couch right now with a candle going, and I literally paused this trashy dating show because my heart dropped reading that. First things first, I want you safe tonight. If you’re parking somewhere, aim for somewhere lit and low‑key—near a 24‑hour grocery or a hospital lot tends to feel a bit safer. Crack the windows just a touch, keep your phone charging if you can, and try to have a hoodie or blanket in reach. I know you didn’t ask for tips, but I’m thinking about you staying okay till morning.

If you want me to pull a quick lifeline, I might actually know something that could help with a place. Carriage Town Ministries in Flint has been solid for people I know—sometimes they can do emergency beds and help you get into longer‑term housing. I can share the details or even call and see what’s up and then text you the info, whatever’s easier for you. No pressure—just putting it on the table.

Also, I’m proud of you for staying clean through this. For real. That takes grit most people don’t have, especially when everything’s chaotic. You’ve already shown you can hold your line when it’s messy, and that matters here too.

I’ve got a little time tonight—I can help you map out a quick plan for the next 24–48 hours and tap a couple more options. And if you just need to vent for a second, I’m here for that too. I’m not letting you shoulder this alone.
